study.title: Darker radar, dry ground
study.place: Gandak basin, West Champaran · Bihar, India
study.question: What changed—and how strong is the evidence?
study.summary: Between Sep 12 and Oct 6, 18 units darkened by 3 dB or more. All 18 are visibly dry in an independent Oct 6 image. The darkness-tested baseline flags none of them; exposed water on Oct 6 is limited to 0.27 km² of thin channel threads.

metrics.scope: Oct 6 exposed-water visibility check over every 90 m unit in the AOI (30102 units; census, not a probability sample). Target = exposed water visible on Oct 6 (not NEW water: the Sep 13 view is too cloudy). Recall and FN therefore include persistent water the change detector is not designed to flag.
metrics.uncertaintyNote: Adjacent units are spatially correlated and there is one event/region; no confidence interval is reported. Counts describe this AOI only. Per-block counts are in the run manifest.

provenance.method: Two-date HH detector on NISAR GCOV: 10·log10 of 3×3 power-domain means on the HLS 30 m grid; candidate = Δ ≤ drop AND Oct 6 ≤ dark. Mandatory exclusions: GCOV mask 0/255 on either date and non-positive power. Thresholds are proposed starting values, not tuned (no development labels exist).

sources.title: NISAR L2 GCOV provisional (ASF DAAC), doi:10.5067/NIL2GCOV-P1
Xu (2006) MNDWI, Int. J. Remote Sensing 27(14)

limitations: Provisional NISAR products (CRID P05023); calibration is not validated by NASA for this maturity.
The original probe box near Bagaha lay 100% outside the radar swath (mask 255) and was rejected; the Gandak main channel there is outside track 098.
Sep 13 optical is ~18% clear over the AOI, so new-water reference labels are almost entirely unavailable; no accuracy claim for flood (new water) detection is made.
Thresholds are proposed, not tuned; the sensitivity table shows how mapped candidate area depends on them.
24-day interval spans the post-monsoon harvest; crop and soil-moisture change are competing explanations for darkening.
Optical evidence cannot establish absence of water below canopy. Unknown is not dry, and no-change is not safe.
Mapped candidate area is an algorithm output, not an estimated inundated area.
isUrgentObservation differs (before True, after False); recorded, not a geometry/calibration gate.
steps: Select a catalogue pair with identical track, frame, look, release and bandwidth (NISAR L2 GCOV, provisional).
Reject areas outside the radar swath (GCOV mask 255); choose the area by coverage and Oct 6 optical visibility only.
Read bounded HDF5 subsets; exclude mask 0/255 and non-positive power on either date; verify identical grids.
Average HH power in 3×3 blocks onto the HLS 30 m grid, then convert with 10·log10 (never average dB).
Flag candidates where ΔHH ≤ -3.0 dB and Oct 6 HH ≤ -15.0 dB (proposed thresholds; sensitivity reported).
Label 90 m units from HLS Fmask (cloud/shadow excluded) and MNDWI > 0; mixed or cloudy units stay unknown.
Derive acquisition geometry at zero Doppler from the GCOV orbit state vectors; check look side against metadata.
Report counts with denominators; choose illustrative sites only after the census.

notShown: Flood (new-water) detection accuracy: the Sep 13 view is too cloudy to label new water.
Inundated area: there is no probability sample, only mapped candidate area.
Water under vegetation: optical imagery cannot see it, so unknown is never treated as dry.

accuracy.scope: Open-water presence on 2026-10-06, Kosi barrage reach, 90 m units. Reference: HLS L30 G4348564470-LPCLOUD (MNDWI > 0, cloud-free, 18.9 h before radar). Threshold fixed on development blocks; metrics on 22 held-out blocks. Overall accuracy is inflated by class imbalance; F1 and MCC are the headline. Water presence, not flood (new water). Pre-registered in docs/PROTOCOL_WATER.md.
